objective: Implement the five reader-workflow improvements and pass independent fresh-reader retests for Python, API and native Windows x64 memory checking.
audience: Basic programming/terminal familiarity; concise setup, commands and expected results without excessive handholding.

items.title: Add concrete own-project and own-API next steps
items.acceptance: Starting after the successful demo, a reader can identify exactly what to replace and run a bounded check on a second synthetic project/API without designing the command from a reference manual.

items.title: Complete one Windows memory-checking first-run path
items.acceptance: A fresh reader can verify prerequisites, run the known failure and correction, locate the report, and explain its limits. If setup is unavailable, the next action and support boundary are explicit.

items.title: Clarify and verify the API interpreter requirement
items.acceptance: The prose and command select the same intended runtime; a reader with a different default Python can tell whether to proceed or install/select another interpreter.

items.title: Make Pylint first steps easier to reach
items.acceptance: The reader can reach an installation command, file-check invocation, and output explanation from the start section without locating multiple source citations.

items.title: Explain how to obtain and enter the example directory
items.acceptance: Test acquisition from the published site in a directory without an existing checkout; keep this opportunity provisional until that test.

limits: No merge to main or Pages publication.
No global toolchain installations or host settings changes.
Windows memory execution is native x64 CI; this ARM64 host is not validated.
